chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ate at the home of a family, he would say to them: 'The fasting ones have eaten with you, and the righteous have eaten with you, and the chosen angels have sent blessings upon you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication the Prophet said when eating at someone's house?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this supplication as a model of prophetic etiquette, where the Prophet (peace be upon him) transforms a simple meal into a spiritual event by invoking the presence of fasting believers, the righteous, and the chosen angels. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of hospitality, linking material generosity with divine blessing (barakah) and communal solidarity. It serves as a practical guide for Muslims to elevate everyday acts of hosting into acts of worship through mindful invocation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had a meal with a family, would say to them: ‘The Fasting ones savour the food in your presence, and the righteous eat the food in your presence, and the Chosen Angels send Blessings upon you’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, when eating food with a family would say to them, “Fasting people have received food with you, virtuous people have eaten food with you and chosen angels have prayed for you.’””
